correctness.rationale: The Gram equation on E={0,1,2,3} is exactly six nonconstant Fourier moments plus total weight one. Every six-column moment matrix is independent: after a Fourier exponent shift, the appropriate generalized Vandermonde minor factors into a nonzero Vandermonde and e_3 of six eleventh roots. Its 20 root terms cannot cancel because the cyclotomic minimal polynomial forces equal residue counts, impossible since 11 does not divide 20. Seven distinct nodes yield an invertible ordinary Vandermonde, hence unique real weights. The actual CHECK.py uses rational Machin/Taylor enclosures, integer-scaled trigonometry and Bareiss determinants to check all eight signs in each of 20 dihedral classes, with explicit errors below 10^-7 and determinant margins above 10^-3. Independently enumerated all 330 supports, all 20 orbits, 33 feasible supports in exactly three 11-member orbits, via 65-digit high-precision linear systems. The numerical exercise corroborates the finite certificate but is not itself the certified sign proof.
residual_risks: A high-precision independent check does not establish rigorous determinant signs without the inspected rational interval certificate.
